resources.title: Recall Desk study starter — Study guide
resources.markdown:
# Recall Desk study starter — Study guide

Starter template. Replace the prompts below with source-backed material for your subject.

## Scope and sources

Define the topic, intended use, source dates, and what is outside the scope. If an exam or syllabus applies, record its current version.

- Official outline / syllabus: [fill in]
- Source date checked: [fill in]
- Assessment format and timing, if applicable: [fill in from the source]
- Starting knowledge: [establish through evidence; do not assume mastery]

## Objective map

| Objective ID | Topic | Official weight, if supplied | Evidence still needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | [replace with a real objective] | [do not invent] | [fresh question, explanation, or practical check] |

## Concepts and distinctions

For each objective, explain the rule, when it applies, a close alternative, and a failure case. Cite the specific source section. Separate documented behavior from your own reasoning examples.

State the assumptions, prerequisites, and boundary conditions that determine the answer.

## Worked examples

Use original scenarios with explicit inputs. Show the reasoning, including why tempting alternatives fail. Change one assumption and explain how the outcome changes.

## Applied practice

- Target distinction: [one specific outcome]
- Setup and prerequisites: [smallest useful configuration]
- Prediction: [write before trying it]
- Normal path: [steps and expected result]
- Failure / boundary path: [one changed condition]
- Observation: [what actually happened]
- Exit check: [explain or demonstrate the distinction]

Use an appropriate safe practice environment. Mark unperformed steps as unverified.

## Transfer check

Try a fresh scenario after studying. Record confidence, familiarity, and remaining uncertainty. Keep repeated-question recall separate from fresh application.

## Error log and next action

Topic + mistaken rule: [fill in]

Corrected distinction + fresh evidence / next check: [fill in]

## Reference ledger

| Claim / objective | Document or URL | Section / page | Version / checked date | Direct evidence or inference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [fill in] | [fill in] | [fill in] | [fill in] | [label it] |

resources.title: Recall Desk study starter — Adaptive roadmap
resources.markdown:
# Recall Desk study starter — Adaptive roadmap

This is an undated plan. Study assignments stay provisional until the baseline has been reviewed. [Open the guide](guide.md).

## Phase 0 — Establish a baseline

Complete the diagnostic with confidence and familiarity annotations. Preserve the original answers.

Deliverable: [write an observable result]

Completion evidence: [state what is enough to move on]

## Phase 1 — Review the evidence

Review reasoning by objective. Select up to three active repair targets; keep the remainder parked.

Deliverable: [write an observable result]

Completion evidence: [state what is enough to move on]

## Phase 2 — Repair specific gaps

Read the smallest relevant guide section, predict a changed scenario, and record the corrected distinction.

Deliverable: [write an observable result]

Completion evidence: [state what is enough to move on]

## Phase 3 — Apply the concepts

Use a small lab, exercise, or relevant course activity. Record expected versus observed behavior.

Deliverable: [write an observable result]

Completion evidence: [state what is enough to move on]

## Phase 4 — Confirm transfer and coverage

Use fresh scenarios and acknowledge objectives with insufficient evidence. Avoid treating recognition as mastery.

Deliverable: [write an observable result]

Completion evidence: [state what is enough to move on]

## Phase 5 — Integrate and rehearse

Connect concepts in a complete scenario. Use a fresh assessment and review pacing if relevant.

Deliverable: [write an observable result]

Completion evidence: [state what is enough to move on]

## Optional modules

Select modules from observed gaps; these are not mandatory assignments. Add or remove modules in project.json and link them to guide headings.

- Targeted concept repair
- Small applied check
- Fresh transfer check

## Session note

What changed in my understanding: [fill in]

Next concrete action: [fill in]

## Review before scheduling an exam

Use current source requirements, meaningful objective coverage, and fresh application evidence. No readiness percentage or pass guarantee is implied.
